title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
prompt: You are given a sorted array `nums` consisting of only integers where every element appears exactly twice, except for one element which appears exactly once. Return the single element that appears only once. Your solution must run in `O(log n)` time and `O(1)` space.

examples.explanation: With only one element and no pair to match it, that single element is trivially the answer.

hints: XOR-ing every element together cancels the pairs and isolates the single element, but that's O(n) — the sorted order allows O(log n) instead.
Before the single element, every pair starts at an even index and its duplicate is at the next odd index. After the single element, that pairing shifts by one, so pairs start at odd indices.
Binary search on even indices: if nums[mid] == nums[mid + 1], the single element is to the right of the pair (search right); otherwise it's at mid or to the left (search left).

solution.approach: Before the single element, pairs are aligned so the first of each pair sits at an even index (nums[2i] == nums[2i+1]). After the single element, every pair shifts by one and that alignment breaks. Binary search over even indices only: at an even mid, if nums[mid] equals nums[mid + 1], the pairing is still intact there, so the single element must be further right; otherwise the alignment has already broken, meaning the single element is at mid or earlier. This locates the single element in O(log n) time using O(1) space.
